Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command sources the PKGBUILD file to extract metadata. I examined all top-level code in this PKGBUILD.

The only executable code at the top level consists of two standard shell constructs:
1. `: "${USE_SYSTEMD:=1}"` - The `:` is the null command (does nothing), and this line sets a default value for USE_SYSTEMD if unset.
2. `((USE_SYSTEMD)) || optdepends+=('elogind: sleep and resume notifications through login1')` - This arithmetic evaluation checks USE_SYSTEMD and conditionally appends to optdepends.

Both are normal PKGBUILD patterns for handling optional dependencies. They:
- Do not perform network requests or downloads
- Do not execute eval, base64-decoded content, or other obfuscated commands
- Do not access or exfiltrate sensitive data
- Do not modify system files or execute untrusted code

All other top-level content are standard variable assignments for package metadata (pkgname, pkgver, depends, source, etc.), which are safe.

The build(), package(), and pkgver() functions (not executed during --printsrcinfo) contain only cmake build commands which are standard for this package type.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Top-level code uses standard shell constructs with no malicious behavior</summary>
</security_assessment>
